statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-96237 is a .NET SDK remote code execution issue in workload installation and integrity checking: SDK workload package downloads and integrity-repair paths can bypass NuGet Package Source Mapping, so packages can be fetched again from an unmapped, attacker-controlled feed. Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected and, for the 8.0.1xx feature band, .NET SDK 8.0.100 through 8.0.131 as affected and 8.0.132 as fixed; .NET 8.0.32 ships with SDK 8.0.132 (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/485, https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56613, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build holds a .NET SDK in dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap whose version is 8.0.1NN in build 8.0.NN-r0 (8.0.123 in 8.0.23-r0 through 8.0.131 in 8.0.31-r0, then 8.0.132, 8.0.133 and 8.0.134), and dotnet8-runtime-artifacts holds that SDK's own NuGet packages, among them Microsoft.DotNet.Cli and Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge, at the same SDK version, except that the Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge package in 8.0.25-r0 is 8.0.124. In the x86_64 dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap package, the SDK's command-line assembly dotnet.dll, which implements the dotnet workload commands, reports product version 8.0.131 in 8.0.31-r0 and 8.0.132 in 8.0.32-r0. So 8.0.23-r0 to 8.0.31-r0 carry affected SDKs, and the range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build whose SDK carries the fix.
